extracted.intended_audience: botanists, plant taxonomists, evolutionary biologists, and cytogeneticists
extracted.subtask_description: Morphological, morphogenetic, cytological, genetic and biometric analysis of the polymorphism, classification and geographic distribution of Phyllanthus urinaria, producing a first attempt at systematic units and filiation hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seed hilum configuration and lateral seed ornamentation (Spiralés vs Radiaires)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction of two major subsets characterised by the ornamentation of the seed and the shape of the hilum: Spiralés (S) with often asymmetrical lateral ornamentation and usually a single foveole, versus Radiaires (R) with a more rounded hilum and lateral ornamentation oriented radially from the hilum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This discontinuous character is a major taxonomic discriminator used to separate R and S; details include presence/absence and number/size of fovéoles on lateral faces (S often 1 large or small fovéole; R 0–4 fovéoles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pollen colpi number correlated with ploidy
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of colpi on pollen grains differs by taxon: diploid taxa have 4 colpi, tetraploid taxa have 5 colpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pollen colpi count is tightly correlated with chromosome number (used as a proxy for ploidy): 4 colpi → 50 chromosomes (diploid), 5 colpi → 100 chromosomes (tetraploid). Useful for field/morphological inference of cytotype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chromosome count / ploidy (50 vs 100 chromosomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Variation in chromosome number reveals two cytotypes in studied populations: 50 chromosomes (diploid) and 100 chromosomes (tetraploid, x = 25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cytological classes combine with seed-type (R/S) to define four systematic units: 50R, 50S, 100R, 100S. Chromosome counts (and their correlation with pollen colpi) are primary evidence for delimiting these units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fruit ornamentation types
rubrics_metrics.description: Fruits show marked polymorphism with main types: very scaly (with pilose or non-pilose scales, sometimes coalescent bases), scaly (fewer/less crowded scales, more fleshy), rugose (with more or less protruding mamelons), and smooth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrary to some prior generalizations for Phyllanthus, in P. urinaria fruit ornamentation is considered taxonomically valuable; used together with seed characters to discriminate taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant habit and architecture (erect vs sub-horizontal / orthotropic vs plagiotropic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plants occur with erect habit or sub-horizontal/rampant habit where orthotropic axes tend to root upon contact with the soil; branching (secondary orthotropic branches) varies and affects overall aspect (e.g., bushy vs sparse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Port (habit) is a diagnosable morphological character; in some units (e.g., 50R) erect vs sub-horizontal forms (50R1 vs 50R2) show marked morphological differentiation. Architectural observations include presence/behaviour of plagiotropic rameaux and bud development sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaf morphological traits (size, number, color, shape)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaf characters vary by taxon: size (large vs small; threshold examples given like < ~15 mm^2), number on a given R.P. (range 7–42), color (light green, dark green, frequently anthocyanin-loaded), and shape (ellipsoid to more rounded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaf traits are especially discriminant in regions where gross morphological differences are reduced (colonized areas); foliar measurements are used in biometric analyses and correlate with ecological factors (selection by climate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence, number and size of seed foveoles
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeds may have one or several cavities/fovéoles on lateral faces: Spiraled seeds most often have a single fovéole (variable size), whereas Radiated seeds may have 0 to 4 fovéoles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number and size of fovéoles add to the seed-hilum character suite used to classify individuals into R vs S and subtypes; illustrated in plates and used in systematic diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pollen exine ornamentation (scabrous/tectate with batopillar columellae) — constancy
rubrics_metrics.description: The exine ornamentation is generally constant (scabrous, tectate, with batopillar columellae and non-reticulate) across examined individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While exine texture is constant and thus not discriminating among taxa, the number of colpi (see pollen colpi criterion) is variable and diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductive organ details (flower sepal indumentum, colour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor differences exist among populations in floral characters: sepals of female flowers vary in degree of glabrousness and floral pieces show color variation (parts more or less red, anthocyanin presence on rachises).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These floral variations are noted but generally minor; they supplement other characters when distinguishing closely similar populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical vascularization (bilateralization) — limited utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Bilateralization of vascularization in plagiotropic axes (reported in other Phyllanthus) was investigated but not found to discriminate groups in the orthotropic ramifications studied here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anatomical vascularization can be informative in some Phyllanthus, but for the orthotropic branches of P. urinaria it does not provide useful systematic characters; negative result noted as guidance for future anatomical surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of morphology, cytology, genetics and biometrics for classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification is based on combined evidence: morphological/morphogenetic analysis, karyotype/cytology, genetic confrontation via crosses, and biometric analyses of phenotypic variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors present a methodological standard: use multiple, complementary lines of evidence (morphology, cytology, crossing experiments, biometrics) to validate taxonomic units and filiation hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biometric analysis of foliar area as an adaptive indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Biometric analyses show that variation in relative foliar area of the leaf–internode couple corresponds to an adaptive mechanism granting some genotypes ecological flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foliar-area related traits are used to infer ecological selection and to distinguish taxa where gross morphological characters are otherwise similar (useful in colonized regions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic distribution and polymorphism gradients (center of origin inference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum polymorphism (coexistence of 50S, 100S, 50R, 100R) is in South-East Asia (India, China, northern Vietnam); moving away from this center, the proportion of Radiated types increases and peripheral regions (Africa, Americas) often show only erect Radiated forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geographic frequency patterns are used to hypothesize centre of origin, migration pathways and the subset of taxa that colonized new regions (e.g., migrants likely from unit 50R). Use distributional gradients as circumstantial evidence in classification/filiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population structure, homogeneity and reproductive isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural populations are often morphologically homogeneous (founder effect, selfing and consanguineous crosses lead to homozygosity), while adjacent populations in the centre of origin can be morphologically very different; reproductive barriers observed in crossing experiments maintain divergence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Population-level homogeneity implies strong within-population fixation of characters; reproductive barrier strength varies by cross-type and is used to argue for independent evolutionary trajectories (supports taxonomic separation).
